chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I strove in worship while I was a youth, so my father (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O my son, moderate what I see you doing, for indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when He loves a servant, is pleased with him for the little (that he does).'

key_terms.دُونَ: moderate / hold back / be moderate in

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic teaching on moderation in worship according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises his son to avoid excessive exertion in worship, teaching that divine love is often manifested through Allah's satisfaction with consistent, manageable acts rather than exhausting intensity. This narration underscores the Shia principle of *wasatiyyah* (moderation), warning against *ghuluww* (exaggeration) that leads to burnout and neglect of other duties. It highlights that true piety is measured by sustainability and sincerity in daily practice rather than sporadic peaks of effort.
